title: EA Adds 'Don't Delete' Message to Madden NFL 27 in Bid to Keep Players From Making Room Ahead of GTA 6
snippet: EA has added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27, and players can't help but feel the company is begging them not to make room fo...
fullText:
EA has added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27, and players can't help but feel the company is begging them not to make room for Grand Theft Auto 6.Reports of the new in-game notice began cropping up over the weekend, with CharlieIntel relaying their findings online. EA doesn't explicitly mention GTA 6 in the new message, but considering the pop-up features some familiar pink-and-purple colors and sun-kissed palm trees, it's pretty easy to put two and two together.The message encourages Madden NFL 27 users to refrain from uninstalling the game from their devices, promising that those who stick around can look forward to a new update coming Tuesday, November 17. It's a bit beside the point, but we should also mention that, at least based on early screenshots, EA's message includes a typo, writing "awating signal" instead of "awaiting signal." Newer posts suggest it was fixed pretty quickly. Whoops!EA has added a 'Don't Delete!' message to EA Madden NFL 27 ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI's launch The in-game ad says there's an update on Nov 17 for the title, before GTA VI https://t.co/P00NPUVveK— CharlieIntel (@charlieINTEL) November 14, 2026
"Don't Delete!" the Madden pop-up says. "[ENCRYPTED SIGNAL] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17… do not leak this transmission!"There's just no getting around it; the next week is going to be very, very weird for the gaming industry. GTA 6, a decade-in-the-making video game said to bring the biggest launch of all time, has mostly seen every other game clear the calendar just to make room for it. The atmosphere surrounding Rockstar Games' latest is something to behold, and with millions of players still turning up for live-service titles, one can wonder if any of their developers are worried about GTA 6 taking a chunk of their attention.That at least seems to be the case for EA and Madden NFL 27. If a Vice City-themed pop-up in this year's annual football game release wasn't enough to convince you, its official X/Twitter account actually recently doubled down. A November 10 post promoting a November 18 update referenced GTA 6's massive file size by saying, "Don't let 210GB get between you and Your League."It all seems in good fun, but fans say they can't help but feel like EA is doing everything in its power to keep players interested. Some even say it feels like the company is begging them to stay.When one Reddit user asked what the message was related to, one user replied, "It means that EA is terrified of GTA VI's launch." Another said it felt like the pop-up was the publisher's way of saying, "'PLEASE DON'T DELETE MADDEN TO CLEAR SPACE FOR GTA. title: Xbox at 25: My Memories From Across Xbox’s Entire (and Quite Incredible) History
snippet: The first day of my career was October 1, 2002. I’d been lucky enough to get hired by Official Xbox Magazine. The fledgling Xbox console was not quite a year ol...
fullText: The first day of my career was October 1, 2002. I’d been lucky enough to get hired by Official Xbox Magazine. The fledgling Xbox console was not quite a year old, and when I got settled in on the staff, it quickly became clear that Xbox was really about one thing above all else: Halo. I remember being surprised in my first days on the job by what would happen every single day, like clockwork, at 5pm: consoles and TVs would get turned on, Halo would get fired up, and we’d all play a round or two of Capture the Flag on Blood Gulch before we all went home. Fun and friendly banter ensued. Halo was baked into the Xbox’s DNA from the very start.It is one of my very first of many thousands of great Xbox memories. I’ve been lucky enough to have a front-row seat for most of the Xbox’s 25 years, covering the high highs and low lows of Microsoft’s pivot into the living room. It’s been quite a ride since November 15, 2001, and I wanted to mark the occasion by sharing some of my biggest memories with you. And, like everything else with Xbox, it started with Halo.Thank goodness for Combat Evolved, in fact, because most of the rest of that first year of Xbox history was pretty bleak. Lots of C++ spaghetti was thrown at the wall, and most of it didn’t stick. Oh, don’t get me wrong – there were moments! Steel Battalion, Capcom’s batshit-insane mech vertical tank simulator that cost $200 and came with its own custom 40-button controller and foot pedals was quite simply amazing as both a game and piece of hardware and would never get made today. Meanwhile, The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind was the beginning of Xbox becoming a Western-RPG powerhouse. But first-party hadn’t really found its footing yet, as it published stuff like the now-infamous Blinx: The Time Sweeper.But thanks to Combat Evolved carrying the Xbox through its first trip around the sun, things got really interesting in Year Two. It turns out I joined the magazine at just the right time! Halo: Combat Evolved was the biggest very real reason to buy the console in its first year, but its critical second year was defined by three things: Xbox Live, Tom Clancy games, and BioWare. Year TwoXbox Live was a massive swing that connected for a home run. Back then, high-speed internet was far from ubiquitous. In fact, dial-up 56k modems still dominated the American online infrastructure. But Microsoft put a big bet on broadband by putting an Ethernet port into every Xbox. In the first year, that port only got used for Halo LAN (er, System Link) parties, but then, on the one-year anniversary of the system on November 15, 2002, Xbox Live launched. And it was a loud launch in the very best of ways. MechAssault brought an action-first take on MechWarrior to the console audience – including an excellent multiplayer suite – while a faithful port of the PC’s outstanding military FPS Tom Clancy’s Ghost Recon was a perfect fit for the new online service. And all of it was buttery smooth and almost entirely free of latency

title: League of Legends: New Dawn Unveiled With Debut Trailer, Riot Announces Major Overhaul Coming in 2027
snippet: At the 2026 League of Legends World Championship Finals, Riot Games officially unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn. The large-scale update is scheduled for 202...
fullText: At the 2026 League of Legends World Championship Finals, Riot Games officially unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn. The large-scale update is scheduled for 2027 and will bring changes to the game's client, Summoner's Rift, visuals, and gameplay, marking the beginning of a new chapter for one of the industry's most enduring titles.New Dawn introduces what Riot described as an "all-encompassing" update to League, touching almost every aspect of its experience. "This is the start of a new era for League, a new journey," said Paul Bellezza, League's executive producer, in New Dawn's first official trailer. Riot is expected to share the full reveal of New Dawn this coming January.A new look for Summoner's RiftThe announcement came with a trailer shown at Worlds Finals that offered the first glimpse of what League players can expect from New Dawn, and the changes appear to go beyond simple refreshed graphics. The first noticeable change is a redesigned champion selection screen, which looks much closer to the modern interface found in Wild Rift, League's mobile game. The footage also hints at a new or reworked rune system, which seems to have a much bigger impact on the gameplay than ever before. The trailer also showcased updated minions, a new look for Summoner's Rift, redesigned dragons and Baron Nashor, as well as what seem to be new visual effects for many champion abilities. More interestingly, the footage also hinted at gameplay changes that will change how players approach their matches, including major changes to the map terrain that open new strategic consideration — and not only for junglers. Since its launch in 2009, League has seen more than a few major changes, including a rebuilt Summoner's Rift in 2014, a new client a couple of years later, and runes and then terrain changes in the following years. Still, nothing ever came close to the scale of what New Dawn promises to be. For now, Riot is keeping the full extent of these gameplay changes to itself, leaving much of New Dawn's scope to be revealed in the coming months. Leaving the past behindRiot spent part of 2026 looking back at League's history through League Classic, a mode that allowed players to revisit older versions of both the Summoner's Rift and League's champions. However, nostalgia alone proved difficult to sustain. Just a few weeks after its release, Riot announced that the mode would end its current run in January 2027. The experience could return in a modified format in the future, but it demonstrated that revisiting the past is not necessarily enough to keep a game of League's scale moving forward.Now, Riot is looking in the opposite direction. 18 years since League first launched, New Dawn represents another attempt at evolving a game whose identity has been shaped as much by its community as by its developers. But whether players embrace the changes or push back against them remains to be seen

Spoilers for Resident Evil Requiem follow."I would really love to see how her relationship with Leon blossoms," Sant'Albano explained. "I think we have a beautiful mentorship, almost brotherly, sisterly relationship brewing. And I also want to know what happens with her and Emily."Assuming you chose the 'good' ending, Resident Evil Requiem closes with the series' one-liner expert, Leon S. So far, there's been no word on whether she'll stick around for additional entries and eventually stand toe-to-toe with other protagonists like Ethan Winters or Chris Redfield. Judging by the strong impression she made when her debut game launched in February, we wouldn't be surprised to see her back at some point down the line.Sant'Albano knows Grace could survive another run in with mutated monsters after making it through the horrors of the Rhodes Hill Chronic Care Center, but will she ever be dodging chainsaws with carefully timed but stylish backflips? title: GTA 6 Will Do Something the Franchise Has Never Done Before: Encourage Empathy
snippet: Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 features something the franchise has never had before: mechanisms that encourage empathy.Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson a...
fullText: Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 features something the franchise has never had before: mechanisms that encourage empathy.Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson and head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe talked about how next week's Grand Theft Auto changes the formula the series is known for during an interview with The Guardian (via @GameRoll_). Jason and Lucia will surely be able to cause a fair amount of chaos when players take control in Vice City, but in a post-Red Dead Redemption 2 world, they'll have the freedom to be kind, too."Crime is a fundamental part of GTA – at least up until now, it has been," Nelson said. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out."Games like GTA 5 have given players playgrounds and characters that can maximize the mayhem. Trevor, one of that game's three protagonists, is a great example of this chaotic energy, but in GTA 6, there doesn't seem to be a direct equivalent. Sure, Rockstar's trademark tone and instantly recognizable characters can be seen all over what few trailers we've received thus far, but everything seems a bit more grounded, too.Falling in line with this is the news that GTA 6 will feature a world that might actually reward those who take the citizens of Leonida into consideration. Of course, that doesn't mean those who prefer to wreak havoc won't be able to play their way, too. It just means that, at least based on Nelson's words, there's some room to be a normal or even good person, too."I would say so," he replied when asked if the new game would encourage empathy in some capacity. "I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to."Elsewhere in the interview, Nelson described Jason and Lucia as a "younger couple with their backs against the wall," which is why it doesn't make sense for them to "go out and cause as much carnage and make as much noise as they can." This isn't Michael, Franklin, or Trevor, nor is it Niko Bellic. Thankfully, we won't have to wait too much longer to find out just what kind of criminals Jason and Lucia are, or who they can be.GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X | S. With more grounded in-game mechanisms and NPCs that react to weapons, it's clear we're staring down what will likely be the most realistic Grand Theft Auto game so far. It's something that has plenty of fans excited and others nervous. Recent footage shared by Rockstar has highlighted the game's unbelievable graphics. It's something that has IGN writer Jacqueline Thomas excited, even if it does run at 30 fps.

fullText: Critical Role’s TTRPG system, Daggerheart, puts a greater emphasis on story-telling than some of its peers. A year after the core book was released, Daggerheart offered players and Game Masters new options for telling their stories.with the system’s first expansion. As someone who plays a variety of role-playing games on both sides of the GM screen, I’m always hungry for more options. More gear for my heroes to use and more vicious monsters to sic on my unsuspecting players.Daggerheart: Hope and Fear adds a plethora of toys to the toybox, but if you weren’t a fan of the core book, don’t expect this expansion to change your mind.Before diving into what’s new, for those unfamiliar, Daggerheart is a narrative-focused tabletop RPG system. It uses a rather handy card-based approach to help create and manage your characters and does away with the traditional initiative mechanic during combat. One of the most defining mechanics of Daggerheart, however, is its Hope and Fear dice. These two twelve-sided dice, one representing your Hope value and the other Fear, can either cause your checks to earn you a 'Hope' resource that can be used to pull off extra special actions, or give your GM a 'Fear' point that they can spend. A proverbial "wrench in the gears" sort of treat, depending on which die rolls higher during the check. This mechanic also serves as the namesake for the system’s first expansion. fullText: There’s a lot of shooting and driving in Grand Theft Auto missions, they’re kind of your main verbs in the game. You drive, shoot, and drive some more with the possibility of shooting again. They’re not very dynamic as a wireframe, so it’s a good thing that Rockstar leads the industry in storytelling, character, and satire. Missions burst with thematic meaning, every second an opportunity to push someone forward or revel in gags. It doesn’t really matter what you do. In GTA, a mission that largely consists of buying cargo shorts against your will can rival casino heists, mid-air hijackings, and all-out urban warfare.Friend Request is an early storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto V. Tutorials are behind us but Trevor has yet to join the team. Retired crook Michael De Santa is in deep trouble, so he turns to his old accomplice Lester for help. title: PS5 QSSR Updates Revealed for Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and More
snippet: Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.The list of six newcomers joining the sma...
fullText: Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.The list of six newcomers joining the small-but-growing group of supported games was unveiled in a PlayStation.Blog post. In addition to confirmation that incoming updates will add QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution), the post included testimonials from each of the studios' developers, who shared how the tech will impact visuals.When Sony pulled back the curtain on QSSR in October, it came with confirmation that it had already been implemented in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei. Now, we know that Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Remedy Entertainment's Control Resonant, Embark Studios' Arc Raiders and The Finals, Hello Games' No Man's Sky, and Expression Games' Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will soon take advantage of the AI upscaling tech.In the case of Marvel's Spider-Man 2, QSSR is available as part of a new update that's out now."Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now!" Insomniac head of technology Mike Fitzgerald said. "We’re excited for players to swing back into our 2023 title and see QSSR’s exciting image stability and sharpness benefits in both Fidelity and Performance modes."Remedy said QSSR will bring noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail when it launches in a new update in December. Hello Games founder Sean Murray, meanwhile, promised that players can look forward to No Man's Sky looking "sharper, cleaner, and more beautiful" at the "best possible framerate" in the next few weeks. When exactly The Finals, Arc Raiders, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will receive their updates has yet to be announced."With the new QSSR coming soon to ARC Raiders and The Finals, we can deliver increased sharpness, better environmental clarity, and overall visual improvements to even more PlayStation players," Embark said. "We are very happy to see Sony’s continued investment in PlayStation technology translate into meaningful improvements for all players, bringing more immersive experiences across the PlayStation ecosystem."Sony then teased that developers interested in using QSSR are "just getting started." More PS5 games are set to receive similar updates in the coming months, though which titles will join the list remains to be seen.
